inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset

device.name: Go2Arm Lab (Unitree Go2 + WidowX 250s, Isaac Lab)

facts.text: Go2Arm is a Unitree Go2 quadruped base with an Interbotix WidowX 250s manipulator; the repository trains RL policies for it
Isaac-Go2Arm-Flat and Isaac-Go2Arm-Flat-Play are registered with entry_point Go2Arm_Lab.env.manager_env:ManagerRLEnv and the Go2ARMFlatEnvCfg / Go2ARMFlatEnvCfg_PLAY configs
ManagerRLEnv.__init__ takes cfg and render_mode and calls the Isaac Lab base with cfg
step processes the action through the action manager and advances the Isaac Sim scene cfg.decimation times per call
step returns six values: observation, reward, arm reward, terminated, time-out and extras
The configuration sets decimation 4, episode_length_s 20.0 and sim.dt 0.005 seconds
The action configuration has two JointPositionAction terms: 12 leg joints with scale 0.25 and 6 arm joints with scale 0.5, both around the default joint offsets

The policy observation group concatenates seven history terms (base angular velocity 3, joint positions 18, joint velocities 18, last actions 18, velocity command 3, end-effector pose command 7 and projected gravity 3, each with history_length 10) and five privileged terms (base mass 1, end-effector mass 1, joint torques 18, base linear velocity 3 and foot contacts 4)
Termination includes a time-out and illegal contact of the base, thighs, arm links and calves at a contact threshold of 0.5
The repository targets Isaac Lab v2.2.0, an external simulator framework
The package's own install_requires lists only psutil

determinism.notes: the fake's reset(seed) reseeds Python's random.Random and repeats its synthetic observation/reward trajectory; it has no Isaac Sim state to reproduce

gaps: analytic F0: no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, actuators, sensors or noise; the fake updates a synthetic 727-value observation from the action and a step counter
only the configured 20 s time-out is modelled; the contact-based termination terms and the two reward channels' actual values require the Isaac Sim scene and are replaced by placeholders

the fake's action bounds [-1, 1] are a documented placeholder deployment envelope, not a device fact: no text in the clone states an action bound, and the production adapter leaves the manager environment's action space unbounded unless clip_actions is supplied
the fake was not compared with an Isaac Sim run; observations are Python floats of length 727 where the deployment returns policy-group tensors
reset options are accepted and ignored: the fake has no scene options to apply
no hardware is modelled; the e-stop is the SDK's software latch, not a physical stop

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: the bridge refuses step, reset and seed after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the last observation stays readable
